TAUTOLOGICAL.label: Direct radiographic finding match
TAUTOLOGICAL.note: Concept contains the label term itself; no external citation needed.

Drazner2001_JVP.title: Prognostic importance of elevated jugular venous pressure and a third heart sound in patients with heart failure
Drazner2001_JVP.claim: Elevated jugular/central venous pressure (imaged radiographically as distended IVC/hepatic veins with contrast reflux) is a prognostic marker of decompensated heart failure.

Clark2015_CT_HF.title: Computed tomography of acute heart failure: A novel case and literature review
Clark2015_CT_HF.claim: Contrast-enhanced CT in acute/imminent heart failure can show reflux, pooling, and layering of contrast in the IVC and hepatic veins/parenchyma.

Detrano2008_CAC.title: Coronary calcium as a predictor of coronary events in four racial or ethnic groups
Detrano2008_CAC.claim: Coronary artery calcium predicts incident coronary events across populations; correlated with risk-factor burden (age, HTN, T2D, dyslipidemia) and a marker of subclinical atherosclerosis.

Kronmal2007_MESA_CAC_riskfactors.title: Risk factors for the progression of coronary artery calcification in asymptomatic subjects: results from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA)
Kronmal2007_MESA_CAC_riskfactors.claim: In MESA, traditional cardiovascular risk factors including body mass index, hypertension, diabetes, and glucose were associated with incident coronary calcium and progression of existing calcification.

Sharma2017_CAC_HFpEF.title: Usefulness of Coronary Artery Calcium to Predict Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction in Men Versus Women (from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis)
Sharma2017_CAC_HFpEF.claim: MESA analysis found coronary artery calcium associated with incident HFpEF risk, supporting CAC as a heart-failure comorbidity/risk marker rather than a direct congestion finding.

London2003_CKD.title: Arterial media calcification in end-stage renal disease: impact on all-cause and cardiovascular mortality
London2003_CKD.claim: Vascular media calcification is a hallmark of CKD-MBD; thoracoabdominal aortic Ca²⁺ load tracks dialysis vintage and CV/all-cause mortality. (Deprecated for T2D-renal / CKD aortic-Ca²⁺ decisions — superseded by Lehto1996_T2D_medial and Goodman2000_ESRD_CAC respectively.)

Lehto1996_T2D_medial.title: Medial artery calcification. A neglected harbinger of cardiovascular complications in non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus
Lehto1996_T2D_medial.claim: In a Finnish T2D cohort, plain-film medial arterial calcification independently predicted CV, CHD, and stroke mortality — establishing Mönckeberg-type medial calcification as a diabetes-specific vascular lesion visible on imaging.

Goodman2000_ESRD_CAC.title: Coronary-artery calcification in young adults with end-stage renal disease who are undergoing dialysis
Goodman2000_ESRD_CAC.claim: EBCT in 20–30-yr-old ESRD dialysis patients showed extensive coronary-artery calcification (88% in 20–30y group) tied to dialysis vintage and Ca×P product — seminal observation of accelerated vascular calcification in CKD/ESRD.

Block2004_CKD_MBD.title: Mineral metabolism, mortality, and morbidity in maintenance hemodialysis
Block2004_CKD_MBD.claim: In >40,000 hemodialysis patients, elevated serum phosphorus, Ca×P, and PTH independently predicted all-cause and CV mortality — population-scale evidence for CKD-MBD as a driver of vascular calcification and mortality.

Adler2015_pericardial_ESC.title: 2015 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases
Adler2015_pericardial_ESC.claim: ESC guideline: heart failure (chronic congestive states), uraemia, and fluid overload are explicitly listed aetiologies of transudative pericardial effusion; pericardial effusion is a documented cardiac imaging finding in HF, HFpEF, hypertensive heart disease, and pulmonary congestion.

Porcel2013_pleural.title: Pleural effusions
Porcel2013_pleural.claim: Comprehensive pleural-effusion review: CHF is the leading transudative aetiology, and concurrent pleural + pericardial effusion is a recognised presentation of fluid-overload / decompensated heart failure.

Allison2004_crossbed.title: Patterns and risk factors for systemic calcified atherosclerosis
Allison2004_crossbed.claim: Whole-body EBCT in 650 asymptomatic adults across carotid, coronary, thoracic and abdominal aorta, and iliac beds — directly quantifies the cross-bed correlation of calcified atherosclerosis (abdominal-aorta Ca²⁺ tracks coronary Ca²⁺ as components of one systemic process).

Cantin2009_bronchiectasis_CT.title: Bronchiectasis
Cantin2009_bronchiectasis_CT.claim: Radiology pictorial review explicitly cataloguing CT findings of bronchiectasis and its complications: consolidation from infectious exacerbation, tree-in-bud, peribronchial thickening, and mucus impaction. The structural lesion of bronchiectasis is bronchial dilation; consolidation reflects superimposed infection / mucus impaction rather than the disease itself, making the consolidation-in-bronchiectasis link a known clinical-radiologic association (not a direct manifestation).

Long2017_IVC_sepsis.title: Does respiratory variation in inferior vena cava diameter predict fluid responsiveness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Long2017_IVC_sepsis.claim: Systematic review / meta-analysis showing IVC ultrasonography has limited accuracy for predicting fluid responsiveness in critically ill patients (including septic shock) — frames the audit's 'distended IVC' association with sepsis as a confounded / non-canonical sign rather than a direct manifestation of distributive shock (which classically produces a *collapsed* IVC).

Mohler2001_valve.title: Bone formation and inflammation in cardiac valves
Mohler2001_valve.claim: Calcific aortic valve disease shares osteogenic / inflammatory mechanisms with atherosclerosis; aortic Ca²⁺ load co-tracks valvular calcification.

Bos2015_dementia.title: Atherosclerotic calcification is related to a higher risk of dementia and cognitive decline
Bos2015_dementia.claim: Rotterdam Study (n=2364): higher aortic-arch / coronary / carotid calcification associates with incident dementia, independent of classical risk factors.

Schulz2004_osteoporosis.title: Aortic calcification and the risk of osteoporosis and fractures
Schulz2004_osteoporosis.claim: Aortic Ca²⁺ load inversely associates with bone mineral density; shared aging biology between vascular calcification and bone loss.

Sin2003_COPD.title: Why are patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease at increased risk of cardiovascular diseases?
Sin2003_COPD.claim: COPD/chronic bronchitis and atherosclerosis share systemic inflammation and smoking; aortic Ca²⁺ is a co-morbidity marker, not an airway-disease imaging feature.

DeTorres2007_emphysema_lung_cancer.title: Assessing the relationship between lung cancer risk and emphysema detected on low-dose CT of the chest
DeTorres2007_emphysema_lung_cancer.claim: Emphysema detected on low-dose chest CT was associated with increased lung cancer risk after adjustment for age, sex, smoking history, and airway obstruction.

Beigel2013_IVC.title: Noninvasive evaluation of right atrial pressure
Beigel2013_IVC.claim: IVC diameter and collapsibility correlate with right atrial pressure; large/non-collapsing IVC indicates elevated CVP / right-sided HF or volume overload.

Stawicki2009_IVC.title: Intensivist use of hand-carried ultrasonography to measure IVC collapsibility in estimating intravascular volume status
Stawicki2009_IVC.claim: Distended, non-collapsing IVC in critical care correlates with elevated CVP; in shock states the IVC pattern informs volume status (distributive/hypovolemic typically collapsed, cardiogenic/obstructive distended).

Sagrista1999_pericardial.title: Long-term follow-up of idiopathic chronic pericardial effusion
Sagrista1999_pericardial.claim: Pericardial effusion is a well-characterised cardiac imaging finding; aetiologies include heart failure, fluid overload, uraemia, infection, malignancy.

Light2002_pleural.title: Pleural effusion
Light2002_pleural.claim: Pleural effusion is a direct radiographic manifestation of heart failure (transudate from increased pulmonary capillary pressure) and of pneumonia (parapneumonic exudate).

Sahn2007_parapneumonic.title: Diagnosis and management of parapneumonic effusions and empyema
Sahn2007_parapneumonic.claim: Pleural effusion accompanying pneumonic consolidation is a direct radiographic finding of parapneumonic effusion / empyema.

Davies2010_BTS.title: Management of pleural infection in adults: British Thoracic Society Pleural Disease Guideline 2010
Davies2010_BTS.claim: Empyema imaging hallmarks: loculated pleural fluid, adjacent lower-lobe consolidation, indication for chest drain placement.

Walker2012_pleural.title: Tumorlike conditions of the pleura
Walker2012_pleural.claim: CT differential of pleural lesions and effusions; documents the spectrum of pleural disease imaging.

Kuhlman1997_pleuralCT.title: Complex disease of the pleural space: radiographic and CT evaluation
Kuhlman1997_pleuralCT.claim: Pleural effusion produces adjacent (compressive / passive) atelectasis on CT — a directly observable radiographic sequence.

Franquet2018_pneumonia.title: Imaging of community-acquired pneumonia
Franquet2018_pneumonia.claim: Lobar / patchy consolidation with air bronchograms and ground-glass opacities are direct CT manifestations of community-acquired pneumonia.

Sheard2012_ARDS.title: Imaging of acute respiratory distress syndrome
Sheard2012_ARDS.claim: Bilateral, gradient-distributed ground-glass opacities and consolidation on CT are the canonical imaging signature of ARDS / acute respiratory failure.

Cusack2023_sepsis_ARDS.title: Endothelial dysfunction triggers acute respiratory distress syndrome in patients with sepsis: a narrative review
Cusack2023_sepsis_ARDS.claim: Sepsis is a major cause of ARDS and can drive acute lung injury through endothelial dysfunction, supporting diffuse lung-injury concepts as sepsis-related but non-specific confounds.

Storto1995_PE.title: Hydrostatic pulmonary edema: high-resolution CT findings
Storto1995_PE.claim: Hydrostatic pulmonary edema on HRCT shows ground-glass opacification, smooth interlobular septal thickening, and consolidation; supports CT diagnosis of cardiogenic edema.

Valvani2019_postobstructive.title: Postobstructive pneumonia in lung cancer
Valvani2019_postobstructive.claim: Postobstructive pneumonia can complicate lung cancer, especially advanced disease, and is evaluated with imaging; consolidation is therefore a disease-related confound rather than a direct tumor-mass finding.

DeWever2011_crazypaving.title: The crazy-paving pattern: a radiological-pathological correlation
DeWever2011_crazypaving.claim: Crazy-paving = ground-glass + superimposed interlobular septal thickening; the GGO-with-septal-thickening motif is the pathological correlate of interlobular septal thickening labels.

Hansell2008_Fleischner.title: Fleischner Society: glossary of terms for thoracic imaging
Hansell2008_Fleischner.claim: Canonical definitions of HRCT terms: peribronchial / peribronchovascular thickening, bronchiectasis, consolidation, ground-glass opacity, mosaic attenuation, septal thickening.

Silva2009_ileus.title: Small bowel obstruction: what to look for
Silva2009_ileus.claim: Dilated, fluid-filled small-bowel and colon loops on CT are direct radiographic findings of mechanical obstruction or paralytic ileus.

Roussos2007_hydrothorax.title: Hepatic hydrothorax: pathophysiology, diagnosis and management
Roussos2007_hydrothorax.claim: Ascites can produce ipsilateral pleural effusion (hepatic hydrothorax) via diaphragmatic defects — a known clinical / pathophysiologic association linking ascites and pleural effusion on imaging.

Krok2014_hydrothorax.title: Hepatic hydrothorax: current concepts
Krok2014_hydrothorax.claim: Hepatic hydrothorax review: ascites → pleural effusion through transdiaphragmatic communication; right-sided predominance.
